newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb damages shipping company offices in Marseille.
newsitem.headline: Bomb damages shipping company offices in Marseille.

text.p: A powerful bomb exploded early on Thursday outside the headquarters of a shipping company in France's Mediterranean port of Marseille, police said.
No one was hurt but the building was extensively damaged, they said.
The offices belonged to SNCM, the main shipping company serving the troubled French Mediterranean island of Corsica.
French radio said another explosion in Limoges, central France, overnight caused extensive damage to a courthouse. No casualties were reported.
No one has claimed responsibility for either attack.

Corsican separatists have claimed responsibility for several attacks against administrative buildings in mainland France in the past two months, including the town hall in Bordeaux where Prime Minister Alain Juppe is the mayor.
Police said a bomb blast early on Wednesday in an empty mess at the French Air Force's Solenzara base in Corsica caused slight damage but no casualties.

No one claimed responsibility for the bombing, which occurred one day after the clandestine Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC-Canal Historique) said it had carried out nine attacks and one attempted attack against civilian targets on the island since October 25.
